result.instructions: Mesh Control Engine editor. One project per process. Scenes are .mcscene documents of entities (id, name, reflected components). Discover component types with refl_list_components / refl_describe_component; read with scene_info, scene_list_entities, scene_get_entity, asset_list; edit with entity_* and component_* (values use the .mcscene spelling: vectors as arrays, assets as "guid:<uuid>", entity references as "$<entity id>", enums by name). Edits stay in memory until scene_save. Verify with cook_run, cook_errors and run_headless (deterministic: same scene + ticks = same state_hash). Docs, samples and examples: mce://docs/index, docs_search; what is data and what needs code: engine_capabilities; prompts start_game, add_level, polish_pass. Something the engine made hard: report_friction.

tools.name: refl_list_components
tools.description: List every reflected component type (name and field count).

tools.name: refl_describe_component
tools.description: Describe a component type, or a reflected value type such as UiAnchors or UiStyle (runtime UI): fields with kind, array count, nested struct fields, enum values, editor range, read-only/transient flags and help text.

tools.name: scene_info
tools.description: The open scene: name, GUID, path under assets/, unsaved changes, entity count.

tools.name: scene_list_entities
tools.description: List the scene's entities in file order: id, name, component types. Optional component filter.

tools.name: scene_get_entity
tools.description: One entity (by id, or by name when unique) with its component values in .mcscene form (fields at their default are omitted; entity references are "$<id>"; a value you write may also name the entity). Ids are saved in the file and survive scene_open.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: asset_list
tools.description: Assets of the project (GUID registry): guid as "guid:<uuid>", path under assets/, type.

type.description: Texture, Font, Sfx, Scene, Mesh, Material, ...

tools.name: asset_set_import_settings
tools.description: Replace an asset's importer settings in its .mceasset sidecar (texture: {"srgb": bool, "mips": bool, "max_size": 1024} where max_size is a power of two that halves a bigger image before its mips, to shrink the pack; a normal map or LUT needs srgb false; video (.mpg): {"audio": bool, "normalize": bool}). Keys are validated by the next cook_run.

tools.name: entity_create
tools.description: Create an entity (with a LocalTransform unless transform is false) and optionally components, e.g. {"Sprite": {"texture": "guid:...", "size": [1, 1]}}. With 'prefab', an instance of that .mcprefab whose 'components' override the prefab root's fields (LocalTransform places it). An entity reference field takes "$<id>", the entity's unique name, or null. Returns its id.

prefab.description: "guid:<uuid>" of a .mcprefab: place an instance; components then override the prefab root's fields

at.description: Index in the hierarchy; default: the end

tools.name: entity_delete
tools.description: Delete an entity and its children. Entity references to them from other entities become null: the result lists each as nulled_links (owning entity, component, field) so you can set them again or scene_undo.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: scene_clear
tools.description: Delete every entity of the open scene (one undo step): re-author a scene keeping its GUID and path.

tools.name: entity_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate an entity right after itself. Returns the new id(s).

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_add
tools.description: Add a component (default values, or patched with 'value': an object of fields).

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_remove
tools.description: Remove a component from an entity.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_set
tools.description: Change a component. Without 'path', 'value' is an object of fields to change. With a property path ("position", "position.x", "shape.half", "items[2]"), 'value' is that property's value. An entity reference takes "$<id>", the entity's unique name, or null. Type errors name the expected type.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: scene_new
tools.description: Start a new, empty, unsaved scene (refuses to drop unsaved changes unless force).

tools.name: scene_open
tools.description: Open a .mcscene, or a .mcprefab to edit the prefab itself (entity 0 is its root), by its path under assets/. Always re-reads the file from disk (also when it is already open), so it shows what other agents saved; it refuses to drop unsaved changes unless force.

tools.name: scene_save
tools.description: Save the scene (atomic write; entity ids are saved with it). With 'path' (under assets/): save as, with a fresh GUID for a new file. 'name' renames the scene. When another agent saved the file since it was opened, their edits are merged in entity by entity (their new entities are kept); edits to the same component of an entity conflict and nothing is written unless resolve picks a side. When the file cannot be merged the error names the entities on disk your copy lacks: scene_open with force reloads it, or overwrite: true saves yours over it. Refuses to overwrite another existing file unless force (an overwritten file keeps its GUID; force skips the merge). A path ending in .mcprefab saves the document as a prefab (entity 0 is the root; prefab_create_from makes one from an entity).

overwrite.description: Save over the file even if another agent changed it; their edits are lost

tools.name: navmesh_bake
tools.description: Bake the scene's first NavMeshSurface3D into assets/navmesh/<scene>/nav_<entity id>.mcnav from the colliders (and, with include_meshes, the meshes) on its layer_mask, with its NavArea3D volumes and NavLink3D links, and point the surface's 'baked' at it (scene_save keeps that). Re-baking overwrites the same file and GUID. Returns the asset, its content_hash (the same scene bakes byte-identical), the tile grid, layers, input triangles and bytes. Without a baked asset the surface is baked when the scene starts.

tools.name: scene_undo
tools.description: Undo the last scene edit (one tools/call is one step; editor edits share the history).

tools.name: scene_redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone scene edit.

tools.name: cook_run
tools.description: Cook the project (incremental) into <project>/cooked. pack: also write <project>/assets.mce (a host built from the project plays its own build-tree pack unless started with -pack <that file or the cooked dir>; `mce play` and `mce headless` run build/project/assets.mce, which only `mce build` refreshes). adopt: give new source files (a PNG, WAV, TTF or .luau added under assets/ with no .mceasset sidecar) a sidecar with a fresh GUID instead of a cook error (the error for such a file says to call this with adopt: true). paths: project-relative asset files or folders under assets/ (e.g. ["scenes/level_02.mcscene", "textures/"]); cook only those and what they depend on, check nothing else, and leave the rest as it was; it cooks into cooked/ only and never rewrites the pack (a pack must hold the whole project), so pack is ignored with paths; an entry that matches no asset is an error. skip_errors: also return failed_files, every file that could not be cooked with its first error (assets that depend on a failed one are blocked); the rest still cooks, as it does without skip_errors, but the pack is written only by a run with no errors. A scene component or field the loaded module does not know fails the cook: rebuild the module (module_build, or `mce build`) and restart the server if it was not started with --module. max_texture_size: cap the largest side of PNG/JPG textures at this many pixels (a power of two, 1..16384; default no limit) so the pack shrinks: bigger ones are box-halved before their mips, a sidecar "max_size" (asset_set_import_settings) smaller than it wins; changing it re-cooks the textures. Returns counts, diagnostics with file:line, the output paths (relative to the project folder) and sizes: cooked bytes by type (textures, meshes, audio, scenes, other), the five largest assets, and how many textures the cap downscaled.

max_texture_size.description: Cap on a PNG/JPG texture's largest side, a power of two; default no limit

tools.name: cook_errors
tools.description: Diagnostics of the last cook (file, line, col, stage, message).

tools.name: asset_delete
tools.description: Delete a source file under assets/ together with its .mceasset sidecar and its CREDITS.md row (a font's license text too when no other font of its family is left; not the open scene). The catalog is rescanned.

tools.name: run_headless
tools.description: Cook, then play the saved scene headless for N fixed ticks exactly as the game's host plays it with -headless (the game's own systems included in a project server), or another saved scene of the project with 'scene'. Returns the World state_hash (same scene + ticks + input = same hash), World metrics and the log tail. input: scripted keyboard/gamepad actions per tick, as the game reads them from InputState ("Move" [x,y], "Jump", "Fire", "Pause", "Confirm", "Cancel" and any game-defined action name); a press is a one-tick segment, a hold a range. inspect: after the last tick, report the live component values (Transient runtime fields included) of scene entities by id and/or of every entity with a component (at most 64); show picks the components to print. trace: component fields of scene entities every N ticks, as series (how a value moved over the run, not only where it ended).

scene.description: Play this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one; inspect then takes 'component' only

convars.description: Console variables for this run, name -> value (e.g. {"lc.quality": 0}); put back after it

input.description: Either a script string, one segment per line: "<from>[-<to>] Action[=value] ..." (e.g. "10-70 Move=1,0 Jump\n100 Fire"), or an array of segments

actions.description: Action name -> true, a number, or [x, y]

component.description: Every live entity with this component (also ones the run spawned)

show.description: Components to print (default: the entity's scene components, or the filter component + LocalTransform)

trace.description: Sample fields during the run: {"every": ticks (10), "fields": [{"entity": id or name, "field": "LocalTransform.position.x"}]} (at most 16 fields, 1000 rows)

tools.name: console_list
tools.description: List console variables (type, value, flags, help) and console functions. Optional name prefix.

tools.name: console_exec
tools.description: Execute one console line ("name" prints, "name value" sets, "func args" calls). Cheat and restart-only variables are refused unless the server runs with --allow-cheats.

tools.name: render_frame
tools.description: See the game: draw the open (saved) or another saved scene with the real player at sim tick N, with scripted input, from its own camera or another, at a chosen size and safe area. Returns the frame as a PNG image. Works without a GPU (offscreen software rendering). 'save' also writes the PNG under the project folder.

tick.description: Capture the first frame after this sim tick

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

camera.description: Render from another camera (render only, the sim is unchanged): {"entity": id or name} of a camera entity in the open scene, {"index": n} (scene entity index), {"position": [x,y,z], "target": [x,y,z], "fov": deg} (free 3D) or {"center": [x,y], "zoom": z} (free 2D). A camera object also takes (alone, it keeps the scene's own camera) "focus" (depth of field: meters to the sharpest plane, or "target" = the distance from position to target) and "exposure" (a multiplier of the scene exposure)

view.description: Look at one local player's view or one render texture's camera (M-VIEWS), full size: {"player": 1..4} or {"texture": entity id or name}. Join the players with input ("5 P2/Join") so their cameras follow them. Not with camera

environment.description: Override Environment3D fields for this shot only (the scene is unchanged): numbers, true/false for flags, [x,y,z] / [r,g,b] for vectors and colors, e.g. {"fog_density": 0.04, "sun_color": [1, 0.6, 0.3], "depth_of_field": 1} (refl_describe_component Environment3D lists the fields)

safe_area.description: Pretend the screen has these safe-area insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: UI lays out inside them and the image outlines them

software.description: Force the offscreen software renderer (automatic when there is no display)

convars.description: Console variables for this run, name -> value (e.g. {"lc.quality": 0}): preview a setting without changing the project

save.description: Also write the frame as a PNG at this path inside the project folder, e.g. shots/title.png

tools.name: render_sheet
tools.description: A contact sheet: frames at several ticks (columns) from one or more cameras (rows) in one image, each cell labelled with its tick. One player run per camera.

cameras.description: Camera objects as render_frame's 'camera'; default: the scene's own

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

camera.description: Render from another camera (render only, the sim is unchanged): {"entity": id or name} of a camera entity in the open scene, {"index": n} (scene entity index), {"position": [x,y,z], "target": [x,y,z], "fov": deg} (free 3D) or {"center": [x,y], "zoom": z} (free 2D). tools.name: timeline_preview
tools.description: See a cutscene at a moment: draw the scene with every timeline in it paused at 'time' seconds (state tracks applied, cinematic cameras placed, the timeline's video frame shown) with the real player, as render_frame does. Returns the frame as a PNG image; 'save' also writes it under the project folder.

tools.name: image_diff
tools.description: Compare a frame with a golden PNG in the project: 'image' (a PNG in the project) or 'render' (render_frame's arguments). Returns the score (mean channel difference, 0..1), the changed fraction and pass (score <= max_score), with a heat map image. With no golden yet, or update: true, the image becomes the golden.

golden.description: PNG path inside the project folder, e.g. goldens/title.png

image.description: PNG path inside the project folder to compare

render.description: render_frame arguments: the frame to compare

tick.description: Capture the first frame after this sim tick

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

threshold.description: Channel difference a pixel may have and still count as unchanged

update.description: Write the image as the new golden

tools.name: perf_run
tools.description: Measure a scene with the real player: N frames at one sim tick per frame (counters repeat run to run), judged against a target's performance budget (project_get budgets_in_force). Returns the verdict with advice for each limit over, frame/sim/render/GPU ms (p50/p95/p99/max), draws, triangles, sprites and other counters, the slowest systems, the GPU stages, and spike frames with their cause. The .mcperf capture is kept (cooked/.perf/last.mcperf, or 'save'); perf_compare compares two. Works without a GPU (software rendering; times are then the CPU's). headless: true measures the sim alone.

scene.description: Scene path under assets/ (default: the open scene, saved)

warmup.description: Frames run first and left out (loading, first uploads)

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

convars.description: Console variables for this run, name -> value (e.g. {"lc.quality": 0}): preview a setting without changing the project

save.description: Also keep the capture at this path in the project folder, e.g. perf/before.mcperf

tools.name: perf_compare
tools.description: Compare two .mcperf captures (default: perf_run's last two): p50/p95 of frame, sim, render and GPU ms, the worst frame's counters, the systems whose ms per frame moved most, which metrics got better or worse, and the after capture's verdict against the target's budget.

before.description: Path in the project folder (default cooked/.perf/previous.mcperf)

tools.name: module_build
tools.description: Rebuild the game module with the project's CMake build (the tree the loaded module came from) and map the new build into this server: new and changed components and systems are live for the next tool call, no restart. Returns the compiler's errors (and with warnings: true its warnings) as {severity, file, line, col, message}, plus the output's end when the build failed. The open scene is kept (re-read with the new layouts); the undo history restarts.

reload.description: Map the new build after a successful build

tools.name: module_test
tools.description: Run the project's tests with ctest in the module's build tree (default filter: tests named <game>_*, such as the <game>_headless_300 smoke test). Builds the host and the cooked pack first, so the tests play the current content. Returns each test's result and the output's end when one failed.

tools.name: test_run
tools.description: Run playtest scenarios without a person: .mctest files (JSON) under the project's tests/ folder, one file or folder ('path'), or one inline scenario ('test'). A scenario plays a saved scene headless with scripted input or a built-in bot, may stop early ('until'), and checks component fields (at the end or at a tick), entities alive, event counts, the log and the bot's feel metrics. Returns each scenario's checks with actual values, its state_hash, and the feel report (time to finish, deaths, stuck spots, idle time) when it has an actor.

path.description: A .mctest file or a folder of them inside the project (default tests/)

test.description: One scenario inline, in the .mctest format: {name, scene, ticks, input | bot, actor, until, death, assert: [checks], trace}

tools.name: playtest
tools.description: Let a built-in bot play the scene and say how it felt: walk_to (head for a point or entity, jumping or sidestepping when stuck), explore (seeded random wandering, coverage) or masher (random button chords, crash and soft-lock hunting). Returns the feel report: time to finish, deaths, stuck spots with positions, idle time, distance, cells visited. Needs no game code: the bot drives the game's input actions (Move, Jump, ...).

bot.description: {kind: walk_to|explore|masher, actor: entity, target: [x,y(,z)] or entity (walk_to), through: [waypoints, points or entities or {at, wait: ticks to stand there}, reached in order before target] (walk_to), air_jumps: 0-4 extra Jump presses in the air (walk_to, side view), plane: xy|x|xz (default xy; x = side view with Jump, xz = 3D ground), reach: m (0.5), seed, move: action (Move), jump: action (Jump), actions: [names] (masher), period: ticks (8)}

scene.description: A saved scene under assets/ (default: the open scene)

until.description: Stop early when this check holds (a field, alive or event check)

death.description: Count a death each time this check becomes true, e.g. {entity, field: Health.hp, <=: 0}

trace.description: {every: ticks, fields: [{entity, field}]}: sample fields during the run

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Search the engine's shipped docs (user guide, engine reference), the worked samples and the example games. Returns the best sections with their mce://docs/... resource URI, heading, line and a snippet; read the whole file with resources/read. Start with mce://docs/index.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "camera shake" or "RigidBody2D"

tools.name: engine_capabilities
tools.description: What a game reaches through what: each engine feature with how it is reached today (data: a component; asset: a source file type; mcp: a tool; console; code: needs game C++ or Luau). Scenes, prefabs, UI documents, timelines, skeletons, behaviour trees, terrain and scene changes are data you author through the tools; game rules and custom components are the code. Also lists every component, importable asset type, tool and the convar count. Read this before planning a game, to keep game code to the rules.

area.description: Only this area's features (2D, 3D, physics, audio, input, ui, gameplay, scenes, agent, ...)

tools.name: gen_palette
tools.description: Generate a color palette (dark to light) from a seed and a scheme: analogous, complementary, triad, pastel, earth, neon or mono. Returns the colors as hex with a swatch image. 'save' writes it as a 1-pixel-high PNG strip under assets/.

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_sprite
tools.description: Generate pixel-art sprites: a mirrored, outlined, shaded creature, character, ship, item or blob from a seed, in 'colors' (hex, dark to light, at least 3; the darkest outlines) or a palette 'scheme'. 'variants' puts that many (seeds seed, seed+1, ...) in one row. Returns the frames' rects and an enlarged preview. 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ (nearest filtering, no mips) with its sidecar and a CREDITS.md row.

scheme.description: Palette scheme when 'colors' is not given (gen_palette's)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_pixels
tools.description: Draw a pixel-art image from text: 'rows' is one string per pixel row (all the same length), 'palette' maps each character to a hex color ('.' and ' ' are transparent). For a specific shape (a moth, a lantern, a door) that gen_sprite's seeds will not give. Returns an enlarged preview; 'save' writes the PNG with its sidecar (nearest filtering) and a CREDITS.md row.

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_mesh
tools.description: Make a simple 3D mesh for blocking out a level or a toy-like game: a box, plane, sphere, cylinder, cone, disc or ramp (a wedge rising towards +X), centred on the origin with Y up, 'size' its full extent in metres, in one 'color' with 'roughness'. 'humanoid' is a skinned figure (size [shoulder width, height, depth], default [0.5, 1.8, 0.28], facing -Z, feet at -height/2 so a CharacterController3D's capsule centre is its origin) with 13 bones (hips, spine, head, upper_arm_l/r, forearm_l/r, thigh_l/r, shin_l/r, foot_l/r) and the clips Idle and Walk: an Animator plays them, Ragdoll3D makes it go limp, AttachToBone pins props to its bones. Returns its vertex and triangle counts and a shaded preview; 'save' writes it as a .glb (with its material inline) and a CREDITS.md row. Place it with the 3D kit's MeshRef (and MeshCollider3D).

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_tileset
tools.description: Generate a pixel-art tile set in one row: fill, fill_2, fill_3 (variations), top, top_left, top_right (surface edges), platform and decoration. Styles: grass, stone, brick, dirt, sand, snow, water, wood, metal. Returns each tile's rect and a preview; 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ for a TileMap's tile set.

colors.description: 4 fill colors dark to light, or 4 fill + 3 surface colors (default: the style's)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_texture
tools.description: Generate a noise texture (value, perlin, fbm, ridged, worley; tileable by default) mapped through 'colors' gradient stops, or an equirect sky (kind sky: horizon, zenith and cloud colors, 'clouds' cover, 'stars' density; width = 2 x height) for a skybox or a backdrop. 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ (linear filtering, mips).

colors.description: Gradient stops low to high (sky: horizon, zenith, clouds)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_sfx
tools.description: Generate a retro sound effect with an sfxr synthesizer: a preset (pickup, laser, explosion, powerup, hit, jump, blip, random) varied by the seed, with any sfxr parameter overridden in 'params'. Returns the parameters used (tweak and call again), the length and level, and a waveform image. 'save' writes a 16-bit WAV under assets/.

params.description: sfxr parameters to override, e.g. {"wave": "sine", "base_freq": 0.4, "env_decay": 0.3}; wave is square, saw, sine or noise; the result lists every parameter with its value

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_music
tools.description: Generate a seamless music loop (bass, chords, melody and optional drums) in a scale on a root note, exactly 'bars' bars of 4 beats at 'bpm', at most 60 seconds. Returns its length and a waveform image; 'save' writes a 16-bit WAV under assets/ (set the AudioSource to loop).

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: library_search
tools.description: Search the engine's bundled content library: CC0 models and sounds (Kenney), OFL and MIT fonts, and generator recipes (skies, textures, sprites, sounds, music). Every word must match an entry's id, title or tags. Returns ids for library_add, with license and author.

query.description: Words, e.g. "road corner" or "coin"; empty lists everything

tools.name: library_add
tools.description: Copy a library entry into the project's assets/ (its files, the files they need such as a model's texture, and a font's license text) with fresh .mceasset sidecars and a CREDITS.md row naming the author and license; a recipe runs its generator and saves the result. Default folder by kind: models/, sfx/, music/, fonts/, textures/.

path.description: A folder under assets/ ending in '/', or the main file's new path

tools.name: project_check
tools.description: Check the project before shipping and get findings to act on, each with severity, file, line, message and a fix: cook (assets and scenes that fail to import), references (GUIDs no asset has), unused (assets nothing references), credits (media files with no CREDITS.md row), srgb (data textures imported as sRGB, colour textures as linear), performance (against the target's budget: each scene run headless for ms per tick, images larger than texture_size, scenes whose sprites use more textures than sprite_textures) and accessibility (2D text height in pixels on a 1280x720 screen and its contrast against the background). pass is true when there is no error.

ticks.description: Ticks per scene for the performance check

budget_ms.description: Average sim milliseconds per tick allowed (default: the target budget's sim_ms)

tools.name: ship_build
tools.description: Make the release zip: the project's full CMake build (host, game module and the cooked pack; the module is mapped again), a smoke run of the host headless for 'ticks' ticks, then the SDK's `mce ship` (host, module, engine library, assets.mce, CREDITS.md). Returns each stage and the zip's path; ok is false with the stage that failed and the end of its output. Needs the server of an installed SDK (mce mcp <project>). target "web": the browser build for itch.io instead (`mce ship --target web`, from the engine checkout the SDK came from, for a project under its projects/; needs the Emscripten SDK and Playwright): it plays 'ticks' ticks in headless Chromium and returns the zip, the state_hash, matches_headless (the same ticks run headless in the browser) and a screenshot of the last frame. Desktop with steam_app_id: also the Steam depot for this OS and the steamcmd build scripts (<out>/<Name>-steam; nothing is uploaded).

build.description: Run the full build first (false: ship what is built; desktop only)

version.description: Version in the zip's name (default: the .mceproj's, else the SDK's)

out.description: Folder inside the project for the zip (default dist/)

steam_app_id.description: Desktop: also make the Steam depot and build scripts for this app

steam_library.description: With steam_app_id: the steam_api to ship (default: from the server's STEAMWORKS_SDK)

tools.name: project_watch
tools.description: What the other agents on this project did: the event feed (.mce/events.jsonl), one event per write with agent, tool, path and time, numbered by seq. Pass the last call's next as since to get only new events; others: true leaves out your own. agent is your name (--agent, else the client's name and a suffix).

tools.name: asset_lock
tools.description: Lock a file under assets/ (a scene, prefab, material, texture...) so other agents' writes to it are refused until you unlock it or the lock's ttl runs out. Locking a file you hold refreshes it; an expired lock is taken over.

note.description: What you are doing, shown to the others

tools.name: asset_unlock
tools.description: Release a lock you hold. force: true breaks another agent's lock (the feed records it).

tools.name: asset_locks
tools.description: List the project's asset locks: path, agent, since, ttl, note and whether each expired.

tools.name: task_list
tools.description: The project's shared task list (tasks.mctasks): id, title, status (open, claimed, done, blocked), owner, notes, depends and files, with counts per status.

tools.name: task_add
tools.description: Add a task to the shared list. depends: ids of tasks that must be done before it can be claimed; files: the assets it will touch, so others know.

tools.name: task_claim
tools.description: Claim a task: it becomes yours (status claimed). Without id, the first open task whose dependencies are done. Two agents never get the same task.

tools.name: task_update
tools.description: Change a task's status (done, blocked, or open to give it back) and append a note signed with your name. Only the owner changes a claimed task's status.

tools.name: scene_switch
tools.description: Make another scene the open one, keeping the current one open in the background with its unsaved edits; switching back restores them. scene_save saves the current scene.

tools.name: scene_documents
tools.description: The scenes this server has open: the current one and the ones scene_switch parked, each with dirty.

tools.name: report_friction
tools.description: Write down something the engine made hard (a missing tool, a confusing error, a doc that was wrong, a workaround you had to invent) as a note in the project's friction.jsonl, so the engine's developers fix it. Call it when it happens, before working around it. blocking: you could not finish without a workaround.

area.description: The tool or engine area, e.g. render_frame, physics2d, docs

tool.description: The tool call that hit it

tools.name: asset_schema
tools.description: Describe a JSON source asset type: its fields (type, default, help) and the template asset_create starts from. Without 'type': the types asset_create/asset_write handle (.mcpart, .mcsound, .mcseq, .mctilemap, .mcsheet, .mcskel2d, .mcanim, .mcmat, .mcinput, .mcstore, .mcservices, .mcui, .mcconfig).

type.description: ParticlePreset, SoundSet, Sequence, Timeline, BehaviorTree, Tilemap, SpriteSheet, Skeleton2D, AnimGraph, Material, InputMap, StoreCatalog, GameServicesCatalog, UiDocument, UiTheme, RemoteConfig, Terrain, or the extension

tools.name: asset_create
tools.description: Create a JSON source asset at 'path' (its extension picks the type) with a fresh GUID: the type's template with 'content' fields over it. The document is cooked in memory first; a document the cook refuses is not written and the error names the field. A .mctilemap needs content.tileset ("guid:<Texture>"), columns and rows (the tileset's cells), width and height; its tiles start empty. Returns the path and "guid:<uuid>" to reference it.

path.description: New file under assets/, e.g. effects/dust.mcpart

tools.name: asset_write
tools.description: Change a JSON source asset (by path or guid), keeping its GUID. mode "merge" (default): 'content' fields replace the file's same-named fields, others stay; "replace": the document becomes exactly 'content'. Cooked in memory first: a refused document leaves the file unchanged.

tools.name: asset_read
tools.description: Read a JSON source asset (by path or guid): its path, guid, type and parsed content (scenes and prefabs too).

tools.name: tilemap_paint
tools.description: Paint a .mctilemap (by path or guid) in one call: 'clear' sets every tile first, then 'cells' [[x, y, tile]], 'rects' [[x0, y0, x1, y1, tile]] (inclusive, clipped) and 'fills' [[x, y, tile]] (flood fill of the region holding (x, y)) apply in that order. x right, y up, (0, 0) bottom-left; tile 0 erases, n draws tileset cell n-1. Every operation is checked before any applies. preview: true returns the map as text rows, top row first.

tools.name: prefab_create_from
tools.description: Save an entity and its ChildOf subtree as a new .mcprefab (fresh GUID; the root first, references that leave the subtree nulled) and cook it. replace (default true): the subtree becomes an instance of the new prefab at the same place, parent and transform, one undo step. Returns the prefab's "guid:<uuid>" and the instance id.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

path.description: New file under assets/, e.g. prefabs/enemy.mcprefab

tools.name: prefab_apply
tools.description: Write a prefab instance's overrides (of 'component', or of every overridden component except LocalTransform) into its .mcprefab root and re-cook it: every instance sees the values, and they stop being this instance's overrides. Entity references stay overrides.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: prefab_revert
tools.description: Drop a prefab instance's overrides (of 'component', or of every component except LocalTransform): the fields take the prefab's values again, and a component the prefab root lacks is removed.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: project_get
tools.description: The project's .mceproj (name, title, engine_version, games, plugins, start_scene as a GUID, with start_scene_path, budgets), each target's performance budget in force (budgets_in_force: the defaults with the file's budgets over them) and the open scene's WorldSettings (null when the scene has none).

tools.name: project_set
tools.description: Change .mceproj members: name, title, engine_version (strings), games, plugins (arrays of strings), start_scene (a scene's path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"), budgets (performance limits per target, replacing the file's: {"mobile": {"draws": 300, "frame_ms": 33.3}}; fields frame_ms, sim_ms, render_ms, gpu_ms, draws, triangles, sprites, upload_bytes, heap_allocations, sprite_textures, texture_size; 0 = no limit). Checked before the file is written; other members are kept. A game's host reads start_scene when its build is configured: rebuild it to play the new one.

tools.name: scene_settings_get
tools.description: The open scene's WorldSettings (2D and 3D physics gravity), or null when it has none.

tools.name: scene_settings_set
tools.description: Change the open scene's WorldSettings fields (refl_describe_component WorldSettings lists them), e.g. {"gravity_2d": [0, -20]}; an entity "World Settings" carrying it is created when the scene has none. The stock player, run_headless and play-in-editor apply it at the first tick.

tools.name: ui_list
tools.description: UI documents (.mcui): without 'document', every one in the project with its widget count and the input actions its widgets raise; with 'document', its widgets in order as paths ("menu/play") with kind, text, action, bind and convar, plus its font and theme. A scene shows a document through a UiScreen component.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: ui_create
tools.description: Make a new UI document (.mcui) with a fresh GUID: 'widgets' in the .mcui widget format (asset_schema type UiDocument describes it: name, kind, at | fill | anchors, style, styles, text, action, bind, format, children, ...). Checked by the cook before it is written; saved in the canonical form.

path.description: New .mcui path under assets/, e.g. ui/hud.mcui

modal.description: false: a HUD that never takes focus

tools.name: ui_widget_add
tools.description: Add a widget (with any children) to a UI document under 'parent' (a widget path; omitted: the root), last or at 'index' among the siblings. 'widget' is a .mcui widget object; it starts from the look its kind gets in code. Nav paths in it are paths from the document root.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

parent.description: Parent widget path, e.g. menu; omitted: the root

widget.description: A .mcui widget: {name, kind, text, at, style, action, bind, children, ...}

index.description: Position among the parent's children (default last)

tools.name: ui_widget_set
tools.description: Change a widget of a UI document: 'fields' are .mcui widget keys that replace the widget's own (null removes one, e.g. "action": null). "style" changes the listed UiStyle fields in every state, "styles": {"Hover": {...}} in one state, "nav" the listed edges; one of at / fill / anchors replaces the anchors. Renaming with "name" breaks nav paths that name the old path (the call then fails).

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: ui_widget_remove
tools.description: Remove a widget and its children from a UI document. Fails when another widget's nav still names it.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: ui_theme_set
tools.description: Set the theme a UI document is drawn with: 'theme' is a .mcuitheme (asset_create type UiTheme makes one: a palette, fonts per role, per-kind looks) as a path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"; null goes back to the default look. A UiScreen whose theme is set still wins in the player. ui_preview shows the result.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

theme.description: A .mcuitheme path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"; null: the default look

tools.name: ui_preview
tools.description: See a UI document alone: the real player draws it over a plain background at a viewport size, safe area and UI scale, and the frame comes back as a PNG (offscreen software rendering when there is no display). Bound fields read the open (saved) scene, else the project's first scene. A project that does not cook (a broken scene) or has no saved scene is previewed from the document and what it references alone, with nothing bound ('document_only' forces that and skips the project cook). 'save' also writes the PNG for image_diff.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

safe_area.description: Insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: the UI lays out inside them; the image outlines them

save.description: Also write the PNG inside the project folder, e.g. shots/hud.png

document_only.description: Cook only the document, its theme, fonts and sheets, and start an empty scene (bound fields show nothing)

tools.name: terrain_sculpt
tools.description: Sculpt a .mcterrain (by path or guid) with the editor's brushes: 'op' raise, lower, smooth, flatten (to 'target' metres) or noise, one dab at each of 'points' ([x, z] metres from the terrain's centre in its own space), or along them with stroke: true. Saved at once (the file is cook-checked); the Terrain3D using it re-bakes. Returns the dabs, the samples changed, the height range and the height under each point after the change.

points.description: [[x, z], ...] metres from the terrain's centre, in its own space

hardness.description: 0 falls off from the centre, 1 full to the rim

stroke.description: also dab along the segments between points, a quarter radius apart

repeat.description: run the dabs this many times

strength.description: raise/lower/noise: metres per dab at the centre (default 1); smooth/flatten: 0..1 of the way per dab (default 0.5)

tools.name: terrain_paint
tools.description: Paint a .mcterrain (by path or guid): mode "layer" raises splat layer 'layer' (its TerrainFoliage3D grows there too), "hole" cuts holes (not drawn, not collided, left out of the navmesh), "fill" closes them; dabs at 'points' as terrain_sculpt. Returns the samples changed, each layer's share of the paint (%) and the hole samples.

points.description: [[x, z], ...] metres from the terrain's centre, in its own space

hardness.description: 0 falls off from the centre, 1 full to the rim

stroke.description: also dab along the segments between points, a quarter radius apart

repeat.description: run the dabs this many times

strength.description: layer mode: 0..1 of full weight per dab

tools.name: terrain_import
tools.description: Replace a .mcterrain's heights with a heightmap file under assets/: a .png (8- or 16-bit grey; colour gives its luminance) or raw samples (.r16/.raw 16-bit little-endian, .r8 8-bit; raw_width when not square), resampled to the terrain's resolution. The image's top row lies along -z, its left column along -x. 'range' [low, high] metres maps black and white (default: the terrain's height_range). Holes and splat layers stay.

file.description: The heightmap under assets/, e.g. terrain/valley.png

tools.name: terrain_generate
tools.description: Grow a landscape into a .mcterrain (by path or guid): fBm value noise ('feature' metres across the largest hills, default a quarter of the size; 'octaves', 'lacunarity', 'gain'; 'ridged' 0..1 for sharp ridges) stretched between 'low' and 'high' (shares 0..1 of the height range), an optional 'island' falloff (0..1 of the way in from the edges the land sinks to 'low'), then erosion-lite: 'thermal' passes settle slopes toward 'talus_deg' and 'droplets' of rain carve channels. Deterministic in 'seed'. Holes and splat layers stay (auto rules re-apply only to unpainted terrains).

tools.name: procgen_run
tools.description: Run a level generator from a seed (the same code the engine's ProcLevel and Luau use): kind rooms (BSP rooms and corridors), caves (cellular automaton), walk (drunkard's walk) or noise (threshold of value noise), on a width x height grid (8..512). Returns the level as text rows ('#' wall, '.' floor, 'S' start, 'E' exit), a hash, the floor count and whether E is reachable from S (checked again here, not trusted). Deterministic: the same arguments give the same level. 'count' > 1 tries that many consecutive seeds and lists the failing ones only. 'bake' (a .mctilemap under assets/) paints the level into it with 'floor_tile' and 'wall_tile' (tileset cells, as tilemap_paint). Generator parameters are optional top-level integers: leaf_min, room_min, corridor (rooms); fill_percent, iterations (caves); coverage_percent, turn_percent (walk); scale, octaves, floor_percent (noise); min_floor_percent (all but walk).

tools.name: timeline_create
tools.description: Make a new timeline (.mctimeline: a cutscene or any keyed sequence) with a fresh GUID: 'tracks' (one or more) in the .mctimeline track format (asset_schema type Timeline describes it: transform, property, activation, animation, audio, camera, event, subtitle and video tracks; a track's "target" is "self" or a TimelinePlayer binding 0-7). Checked by the cook before it is written. Play it with a TimelinePlayer component (and a Cutscene for letterbox, hold and skip); timeline_preview shows a moment of it.

path.description: New .mctimeline path under assets/, e.g. cutscenes/intro.mctimeline

duration.description: Seconds; 0 or omitted: the last key's end

tools.name: timeline_add_track
tools.description: Add a track to a timeline, last or at 'index'. 'track' is a .mctimeline track object, e.g. {"type": "property", "target": 0, "path": "CameraRail3D.t", "keys": [{"t": 0, "value": 0}, {"t": 4, "value": 1, "ease": "smooth"}]} or {"type": "subtitle", "lines": [{"t": 1, "duration": 2, "text": "..."}]}.

timeline.description: The timeline: a .mctimeline path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

track.description: A .mctimeline track: {type, target, path, keys | ranges | cuts | lines}

tools.name: timeline_add_key
tools.description: Add keys to a timeline's track (by index, 0 = the first): 'key' or 'keys' in the track's own form (a key, range, cut or line object), merged in by time. The result's length is the timeline's play length.

timeline.description: The timeline: a .mctimeline path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: bt_create
tools.description: Make a new behavior tree (.mcbt: an AI's decisions as data) with a fresh GUID. 'blackboard' declares its keys ({"alert": {"type": "bool", "default": false}, "target": "entity"}); 'root' is a .mcbt node with its children (asset_schema type BehaviorTree lists every kind and stock task; default: a selector over a wait). Checked by the cook before it is written. Run it with an AiBrain component naming its GUID (and a Perceiver to see, a NavAgent3D or PathAgent to move); bt_trace shows what it does. The result lists the nodes by index for bt_add_node and bt_set.

path.description: New .mcbt path under assets/, e.g. ai/guard.mcbt

tools.name: bt_add_node
tools.description: Add a node (with its children) under a composite or an empty decorator of a tree, last or at 'index' among its children. 'parent' is a node index from the outline the tools return (0 = the root). E.g. {"task": "move_to", "key": "home", "radius": 0.5} or {"sequence": [{"wait": 1}, {"emit": "bored"}]}.

tree.description: The tree: a .mcbt path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

index.description: Position among the parent's children (default last)

tools.name: bt_set
tools.description: Change a tree: its 'name'; blackboard keys ('blackboard': name -> type, {type, default} or null to remove); and one node by index: a leaf's 'value' (a task's name, a check's key, a wait's seconds), its members ('fields': name -> value or null, e.g. {"abort": "lower", "radius": 2}), 'replace' it with another node object, or 'remove' it with its subtree.

tree.description: The tree: a .mcbt path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: perception_debug_lines
tools.description: Play the saved scene headless for 'ticks' (default 1) and report every Perceiver the way the editor's perception overlay draws it: its eye and forward direction in world space (forward is the world rotation of the entity that HOLDS the Perceiver applied to -Z in 3D, +X in 2D, so a Perceiver on a child follows the child's world yaw, and a parent that already faces its motion plus a second system that turns the child add up), 'yaw_deg' (0 looks along -Z, 90 along -X), the sight range and angle, whether it sees, its target and last_seen, and 'lines': the cone edges and range arc (yellow), a line to the target it sees (green) or last saw (yellow-orange), each as from/to/color. Use it when a guard looks the wrong way: compare 'forward' with the direction it walks.

tools.name: bt_trace
tools.description: Play the saved scene headless (as run_headless does) and report what one entity's AiBrain did: every 'every' ticks the root's result, the running path (node indices and labels) and the blackboard's values; and each tick a node started running ('started'). Use it to check an AI reacts as meant: the guard leaves its patrol when it sees the player, a utility node switches when health drops.

tools.name: script_check
tools.description: Check a Luau script the way the cook does, without cooking: syntax, state kept outside components, component/event/field names (with a 'did you mean'), removed globals and Luau's type check against the engine's mce.d.luau (a '--!strict' first line asks for strict typing). Returns every problem with line and col. 'definitions': also return mce.d.luau (the cook writes it to cooked/mce.d.luau for editors).

path.description: A .luau file under assets/, e.g. scripts/player.luau

source.description: Script text to check instead of a file

tools.name: skel2d_create
tools.description: Make a new 2D skeleton (.mcskel2d, user guide 7.13) with a fresh GUID and one root bone. Then skel2d_add_bone, skel2d_add_slot, skel2d_add_ik and skel2d_key build the rig and its animations, and skel2d_preview poses it. Play it with a Skeleton2D component (component_add with {"skeleton": "guid:<uuid>"}) and a Skeleton2DAnimator for the clips.

path.description: New .mcskel2d path under assets/, e.g. rigs/hero.mcskel2d

name.description: The skeleton's name (default: the file name)

tools.name: skel2d_add_bone
tools.description: Add a bone, last in the list: parents must already exist (add them first). x, y (metres) and rotation (degrees) are the rest pose in the parent's space, scale a factor or [sx, sy], length the bone's length along its +x (gizmos and IK). At most 64 bones. The importer checks the result; an error names the file position and the bone.

skeleton.description: The skeleton: a .mcskel2d path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

parent.description: The parent bone (omit for another root)

tools.name: skel2d_add_slot
tools.description: Add a slot (a textured quad drawn on a bone; slots draw in the order added, the first behind). Without 'attachments' the slot is one quad: texture ("guid:<uuid>", or omit for a solid quad in the tint), rect [u0, v0, u1, v1], size [w, h] metres, pivot [0..1, 0..1] (0,0 = bottom-left), offset [x, y] in the bone's space where the pivot sits, rotation (degrees), tint [r, g, b, a] linear. With 'attachments' (an array of {"name", "type": "quad" | "mesh", ...} in the .mcskel2d form, asset_schema type Skeleton2D) the slot takes only its tint and 'attachment', the one shown first (null hides it).

skeleton.description: The skeleton: a .mcskel2d path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: skel2d_add_ik
tools.description: Add an IK constraint: 'bones' is the chain, parent first, each the child of the one before (two bones: a two-bone solve; more, or type "ccd": CCD). 'target' is a bone outside the chain and not under its first bone; without it only an IKTarget2D entity drives the constraint. mix 0..1 (default 1), bend "positive" / "negative" (two-bone: which way the elbow bends), iterations 1..64 (CCD), order (constraints apply in order). At most 16.

skeleton.description: The skeleton: a .mcskel2d path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: skel2d_key
tools.description: Key an animation channel at time t (seconds), creating the animation when it is missing; a key at the same time is replaced. channel: rotate (a bone; 'value' degrees added to its rest rotation), translate (a bone; x, y metres added), scale (a bone; x, y factors, default 1), color (a slot; 'color' [r, g, b, a] linear), attachment (a slot; 'attachment' the name shown, or null to hide it) or ik_mix (an IK constraint; 'value' the mix 0..1). 'target' names the bone, slot or constraint. 'curve' is "linear" (default), "stepped" or a bezier [cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2] with cx in 0..1. Give one key's fields, or 'keys', an array of them. 'duration' (seconds; default the last key) and 'loop' (default true) set the animation's.

skeleton.description: The skeleton: a .mcskel2d path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

keys.description: Several keys: each {t, value | x, y | color | attachment, curve?}

tools.name: skel2d_preview
tools.description: Pose a skeleton and return every bone's world transform (the skeleton's space: a, b, c, d, x, y, plus the origin, rotation in degrees and the tip at 'length'). With no 'animation' it is the rest pose; with one, that clip at 'time' seconds (a looping clip wraps), the keyed IK mixes included. 'ik_targets' ({constraint, x, y, mix?} in the skeleton's space) aim constraints as an IKTarget2D entity would. The numbers come from the runtime's own pose functions. Also returns an image: a line drawing of the bones and slot quads (not the textures; render_frame shows those in a scene); render false skips it.

skeleton.description: The skeleton: a .mcskel2d path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

animation.description: An animation to sample (default: the rest pose)

tools.name: asset_import
tools.description: Convert an export of a 2D authoring tool into engine assets, with the same converters as `mce import`. tool "aseprite": Aseprite's JSON export (+ its PNG) becomes a .mcsheet (frames as regions, tags as clips). tool "tiled": a .tmj map becomes a .mcscene plus a .mctilemap per tile layer (solid tiles and rectangle objects become Collider2D boxes). tool "ldtk": an .ldtk project becomes a scene per level (IntGrid cells become boxes, entities become markers). 'file' is a path inside the project (the export need not be under assets/); the assets are written under 'out_dir' (default: beside the export when it is in assets/, else assets/imported). Re-importing keeps GUIDs. Features the engine cannot carry are warnings in 'output'; werror: true turns them into a failure that writes nothing. Needs Python 3.

file.description: Export inside the project, e.g. art/hero.json, assets/levels/cave.tmj, assets/levels/world.ldtk

out_dir.description: Folder under assets/ to write to, e.g. assets/levels

name.description: Base name of the written files (default: the export's file name)

level.description: ldtk only: import just the level with this identifier

tools.name: view_list
tools.description: The open scene's views: every camera with a CameraView (window or into a RenderTexture, viewport, order, split-screen cell, its PlayerCamera), the SplitScreen layout and each RenderTexture with its cameras and the surfaces that show it, plus 'problems' (a texture nothing draws into, a view into an entity that is no texture, a split camera nothing enables).

tools.name: view_add
tools.description: Add a render texture to the open scene: the RenderTexture entity, the camera that fills it (2D with an optional 'fit' [width, height] in metres, or 3D looking at 'look_at') and, with 'show_on', a ShowRenderTexture on a Sprite or MeshRef entity that displays it: a minimap, a mirror, a security monitor, picture-in-picture. Returns the new entity ids.

name.description: Name of the texture entity (the camera is '<name> camera')

look_at.description: 3D: the point the camera looks at

show_on.description: Entity (id or name) with a Sprite or MeshRef that shows the texture

tools.name: player_list
tools.description: The open scene's local co-op setup: the CoopGame (prefab, max players, auto join) and for each player 1..4 their PlayerSpawn entities, PlayerCamera entities and the project's input maps that carry "player": n, plus 'problems' (no CoopGame, a player with no spawn, camera or input map, a camera whose split does not match its player).

tools.name: player_setup
tools.description: Build a local co-op rig in the open scene in one call: a CoopGame (with the 'prefab' every player is spawned from), a SplitScreen, and for each of 'players' (1-4) a PlayerSpawn and a PlayerCamera with its split-screen CameraView. Add the .mcinput maps ("player": 1..4) yourself; player_list then checks the whole rig. Join and leave are the players' Join and Leave actions; 'P2/Join' in a run_headless or render_frame input script joins the second player.

prefab.description: "guid:<uuid>" of the player .mcprefab (needs LocalPlayer and LocalTransform); without one players are coloured squares

mode.description: A top-down Camera2D or a Camera3D per player

spacing.description: Metres between the spawns, in a row about the origin
